surface_case: Elle Reyes, a beloved investigative podcaster, reopens the unsolved murder of a young woman and hunts the powerful man who walked free. As she closes in, someone starts hunting her back — leaking her past, threatening her network. A cat-and-mouse between a crusading journalist and a killer who covered his tracks.
true_case: Elle is not just investigating — she is the executioner. Reader knows from chapter 1 she has killed before: when the system fails, she engineers 'accidents' and clean frames. Her podcast is cover and recruitment — a hidden network of women (a lawyer, a coroner, a hacker) feeds her what the courts ignore. Her new target isn't just guilty; he has figured out what she does, and he's building the case that will expose her. The real question isn't whether she catches him — it's whether she can finish him before he finishes her, without her network, or her own buried first kill, coming to light.
core_question: Will Elle Reyes finish Damien Kroll before he exposes her secret life as a vigilante executioner?
emotional_question: Can Elle protect the people she's built her network with — and justify the blood she's spilled — when the system she despises has always failed the innocent?
book1_promise: The guilty man who walked free will be brought to justice — not by the law, but by Elle's own hand, in an 'accident' the world will never question.
book2_hook: The evidence Kroll built about Elle's very first kill did not die with him. In the final beat, it surfaces in someone else's hands — someone who doesn't want money or a story. They want Elle to work for them. The hunter is now on a leash.
reader_payoff_book1: Elle survives, her network mostly intact, her method proven. But she is no longer invisible — the two-way hunt cost her the one thing she guarded most: secrecy.
